concepts.name: Modulus as distance
concepts.description: |x| is the distance of x from 0, so it is never negative; |x − a| is the distance between x and a on the number line.

concepts.name: Modulus equations
concepts.description: |x − a| = b gives x = a ± b when b > 0, one answer when b = 0 and none when b < 0. With two moduli, think distances or split at the points where each modulus changes sign, then check every answer.

concepts.name: Modulus inequalities
concepts.description: |x − a| < b means x is within b of a: a − b < x < a + b. |x − a| > b means x is more than b away: x < a − b or x > a + b.

concepts.name: Least value of a sum of distances
concepts.description: |x − a| + |x − b| is least, and equal to |a − b|, for every x between a and b. A sum of several distances is least at the median of the points.

concepts.name: Graphs and number of solutions
concepts.description: y = |x − h| + k is a V with its vertex at (h, k). The number of solutions of f(x) = c is the number of times the horizontal line y = c meets the graph.

concepts.name: Nested moduli and |f(x)|
concepts.description: Peel a nested modulus from the outside: ||x − a| − b| = c means |x − a| = b + c or b − c. |f(x)| reflects the part of the graph below the x-axis upwards.

concepts.name: |x| + |y| = k
concepts.description: |x| + |y| = k is a square standing on a corner, with vertices (±k, 0) and (0, ±k): area 2k², 4k points with whole-number coordinates on it, 2k² + 2k + 1 on or inside it.

formulas.title: Modulus
formulas.prompt: What does |x| mean, and what does |x − a| measure?
formulas.formula:
|x| = x when x ≥ 0, and −x when x < 0
|x − a| = distance between x and a

variables.meaning: the point distances are measured from

formulas.explanation: Distance has no direction, so the modulus drops the sign. |x − a| and |a − x| are the same distance.
formulas.commonMistake: Thinking |−x| is negative, or that |x − a| = |x| − |a|.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How far apart are −4 and 9 on the number line?

formulas.title: Solving |x − a| = b
formulas.prompt: How many solutions does |x − a| = b have, and what are they?
formulas.formula:
b > 0: x = a − b or x = a + b
b = 0: x = a only
b < 0: no solution
formulas.explanation: Points at distance b from a lie one on each side of a.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing only x = a + b and losing the solution on the left.

formulas.title: Two equal moduli
formulas.prompt: What is the quick answer to |x − a| = |x − b| (a ≠ b)?
formulas.explanation: x is equally far from a and b, so it is the midpoint. No squaring or cases needed.
formulas.commonMistake: Setting x − a = x − b, which has no solution, and stopping there.

formulas.title: Modulus inequalities
formulas.prompt: What intervals do |x − a| < b and |x − a| > b describe (b > 0)?
formulas.formula:
|x − a| < b ⇔ a − b < x < a + b
|x − a| > b ⇔ x < a − b or x > a + b
formulas.explanation: "Less than" keeps x close to a: one interval. "Greater than" pushes x away from a: two pieces.
formulas.commonMistake: Joining the two pieces of |x − a| > b with "and", which leaves nothing.

formulas.title: Counting whole-number solutions
formulas.prompt: How many integers satisfy |x − a| ≤ b, and |x − a| < b (a, b whole numbers)?
formulas.formula:
|x − a| ≤ b: 2b + 1 integers
|x − a| < b: 2b − 1 integers
formulas.explanation: b steps each side of a, plus a itself; a strict sign loses the two end points.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering 2b and forgetting the centre a.

formulas.title: Least value of |x − a| + |x − b|
formulas.prompt: What is the smallest value of |x − a| + |x − b|, and where is it reached?
formulas.formula: Minimum = |a − b|, for every x from a to b
formulas.explanation: Between a and b the two distances always add up to the whole gap; outside, you walk past an end and come back.
formulas.commonMistake: Setting x = a and x = b separately and taking a value that is too large, or answering 0.

formulas.title: Sum of many distances
formulas.prompt: Where is |x − p₁| + |x − p₂| + … + |x − pₙ| smallest?
formulas.formula:
At the median of p₁, …, pₙ
(anywhere between the two middle points when n is even)
formulas.explanation: Moving x towards the side holding more points shortens more distances than it lengthens, until the points balance.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the mean instead of the median.

formulas.title: The V graph
formulas.prompt: What does the graph of y = |x − h| + k look like, and how many solutions does |x − h| + k = c have?
formulas.formula:
A V with vertex (h, k), arms of slope ±1
c > k: 2 solutions; c = k: 1; c < k: none
formulas.explanation: Moving h shifts the V sideways, moving k shifts it up or down. A horizontal line meets a V twice, touches its tip once, or misses it.
formulas.example: y = |x + 2| − 3 has its tip at (−2, −3) and meets y = 0 at x = 1 and x = −5.
formulas.commonMistake: Shifting the wrong way: |x + 2| moves the tip to −2, not +2.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Where is the tip of y = |x − 5| + 1?

formulas.title: Nested moduli
formulas.prompt: How do you solve ||x − a| − b| = c?
formulas.formula:
|x − a| = b + c or |x − a| = b − c
each positive value gives 2 solutions, 0 gives 1, a negative gives none
formulas.explanation: Remove one modulus at a time, outside first. Each inner equation is a simple |x − a| = d.
formulas.commonMistake: Removing both moduli at once and finding only two solutions.

formulas.title: The square |x| + |y| = k
formulas.prompt: What shape is |x| + |y| = k (k > 0), what is its area, and how many whole-number points does it hold?
formulas.formula:
Square with vertices (±k, 0), (0, ±k)
Area = 2k²
Integer points on it: 4k; on or inside it: 2k² + 2k + 1
formulas.explanation: In each quadrant it is a straight line such as x + y = k. The diagonals are 2k long, and area = d₁ × d₂ ÷ 2.
formulas.example: k = 3: area 18, 12 points on the boundary, 25 on or inside.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking the side as k and giving area k² instead of 2k².

levels.title: Modulus as Distance
levels.description: Read |x − a| as a distance, solve equations and inequalities on the number line, and find the flat bottom of a sum of distances.

blocks.title: A modulus is a distance
blocks.body:
|x| is how far x is from 0, so |−6| = |6| = 6. In the same way |x − a| is how far x is from a, and |x + a| = |x − (−a)| is how far x is from −a.

A distance is never negative, so |x − a| ≥ 0 always, and |x − a| = |a − x|.

blocks.title: Equations and inequalities as distances
blocks.body:
|x − 2| = 5 asks for the points 5 away from 2: x = −3 or x = 7.

|x − 2| < 5 asks for the points closer than 5: one interval, −3 < x < 7.

|x − 2| > 5 asks for the points farther than 5: two pieces, x < −3 or x > 7.

blocks.title: Sum of two distances
blocks.caption: Equality holds for every x between a and b: the graph has a flat bottom there. With more points, the sum is least at the median.

blocks.body: When x also appears outside the modulus, as in |x − 4| = 2x + 1, solve both cases and substitute each answer back. One of them is often false.

levels.title: Modulus Formulas
levels.description: Distances, equations, inequalities, the least value and the V graph.

levels.title: Direct Modulus
levels.description: One-step distances, equations, intervals and graphs.

levels.title: Equations, Intervals and Meeting Points
levels.description: Two moduli, counting integers and the best meeting point.

levels.title: Cases, Counts and Least Values
levels.description: Check cases, count solutions and minimise sums of distances.

levels.title: Advanced: Nested Moduli and |x| + |y| = k
levels.description: Peel nested moduli, reflect graphs with |f(x)|, and count the points on and inside the square |x| + |y| = k.

blocks.title: Peel from the outside
blocks.body:
||x − 1| − 5| = 3 means |x − 1| − 5 = 3 or −3, so |x − 1| = 8 or |x − 1| = 2. Each positive value gives two solutions: x = 9, −7, 3, −1. Four in all.

A value of 0 gives one solution and a negative value gives none, so the count can be 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4.

blocks.title: The graph of |f(x)|
blocks.body: Draw y = f(x), then reflect every part below the x-axis upwards. y = |x² − 9| has a hump of height 9 between −3 and 3, so the line y = c meets it 4 times for 0 < c < 9, 3 times at c = 9 and twice above.

blocks.title: The square |x| + |y| = k
blocks.body: Area = 2k²; integer points on it = 4k; on or inside = 2k² + 2k + 1
blocks.caption: In the first quadrant it is the line x + y = k; the other three quadrants are its mirror images, so the shape is a square standing on a corner.

blocks.body: |x − h| + |y − v| = k is the same square moved to centre (h, v): same area, same number of integer points.

levels.title: Challenge: Nested Moduli and Squares
levels.description: Counting solutions of nested moduli and points on |x| + |y| = k.

questions.question: Kavya’s flat is on floor 5 of a tower in Bengaluru, and her car is parked on level −7 of the basement. How many levels does the lift travel between them?
questions.explanation: The gap between two levels is the distance between the numbers: |5 − (−7)| = |12| = 12.
questions.method: Distance between a and b is |a − b|.

hints.text: The distance between two numbers is the modulus of their difference.
Subtracting −7 means adding 7.

commonMistakes: Computing 5 + (−7) = −2 and answering 2.

questions.question: Solve |x − 4| = 9. What is the sum of the two solutions?
questions.explanation: x is 9 away from 4, so x = 4 − 9 = −5 or x = 4 + 9 = 13. Their sum is −5 + 13 = 8 (always 2 × 4, since the two solutions sit symmetrically about 4).
questions.method: The two solutions are a ± b.

hints.text: Which two numbers are exactly 9 away from 4?
One lies to the right of 4 and one to the left.

commonMistakes: Finding only x = 13.

questions.question: Which of these is the solution of |x − 3| < 5?
questions.explanation: |x − 3| < 5 means x is less than 5 away from 3: from 3 − 5 = −2 to 3 + 5 = 8, ends not included.
questions.method: |x − a| < b ⇔ a − b < x < a + b.

hints.text: Read |x − 3| as the distance from x to 3.
Go 5 to the left and 5 to the right of 3.

commonMistakes: Dropping the lower bound and writing x < 8.
Reading x − 3 as x + 3 and centring on −3.

questions.question: |a + b| = |a| + |b| for all real numbers a and b.
questions.explanation: It fails when a and b have opposite signs: a = 3, b = −5 gives |−2| = 2 but |3| + |−5| = 8. The true rule is |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|, with equality only when a and b do not have opposite signs.
questions.method: Test a pair with opposite signs.

hints.text: Try one positive and one negative number.

commonMistakes: Testing only positive numbers and concluding it is true.

questions.question: Which equation has a V-shaped graph whose lowest point is (2, −3)?
questions.explanation: y = |x − h| + k has its tip at (h, k). For (2, −3) we need h = 2 and k = −3: y = |x − 2| − 3. Check: at x = 2, y = 0 − 3 = −3, and |x − 2| ≥ 0 so y is never lower.
solutionSteps: Tip of y = |x − h| + k is (h, k).
questions.method: Read the vertex from the shift inside and the shift outside.

hints.text: Where is |x − 2| smallest?
The number added outside the modulus moves the V up or down.

commonMistakes: Thinking |x + 2| moves the tip to x = +2.

questions.question: Solve |2x − 7| = 11. What is the positive solution?
questions.explanation: 2x − 7 = 11 gives x = 9; 2x − 7 = −11 gives x = −2. The positive solution is 9. Check: |18 − 7| = 11.
solutionSteps: x = 9 or x = −2; the positive one is 9.
questions.method: Split into the two signs, then solve each linear equation.

hints.text: The inside, 2x − 7, must be 11 or −11.
Solve 2x − 7 = 11 and 2x − 7 = −11 separately.

commonMistakes: Solving x − 7 = 11 and forgetting the 2: x = 18.

questions.question: Find x if |x − 3| = |x + 5|.
questions.explanation: x is equally far from 3 and from −5, so x is their midpoint: (3 + (−5)) ÷ 2 = −1. Check: |−1 − 3| = 4 and |−1 + 5| = 4.
solutionSteps: |x + 5| is the distance from x to −5.
Equal distances from 3 and −5: the midpoint.
questions.method: Equal distances from two points: take the midpoint.

hints.text: |x + 5| is the distance from x to −5, not to 5.
Which point is equally far from 3 and −5?

commonMistakes: Taking the midpoint of 3 and +5 and answering 4.
Halving the gap (8 ÷ 2 = 4) instead of finding the middle point.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x + 2| ≤ 6?
questions.explanation: |x + 2| ≤ 6 means −8 ≤ x ≤ 4. The integers from −8 to 4 number 4 − (−8) + 1 = 13 (that is 2 × 6 + 1).
questions.method: Find the interval, then count its integers, ends included.

hints.text: |x + 2| is the distance from x to −2.
Count the end points too, since the sign is ≤.

commonMistakes: Answering 12 by forgetting to count both ends.
Centring on +2 instead of −2 (the count stays 13, but the interval is wrong).

questions.question: Three friends live at the 3 km, 11 km and 20 km markers on a straight highway out of Pune. They meet at one point on the highway. What is the least possible total distance the three of them travel to get there?
questions.explanation: The total is |x − 3| + |x − 11| + |x − 20|, least at the median, x = 11: 8 + 0 + 9 = 17 km. With three points the least total is always the gap between the outer two, 20 − 3 = 17.
solutionSteps: Least at the median marker, 11 km.
questions.method: Meet at the median.

hints.text: Write the total distance as a sum of moduli.
The best meeting point is the middle friend’s marker.

commonMistakes: Giving the meeting point (11 km) instead of the total distance.
Meeting at one end (3 km) and getting 8 + 17 = 25 km.

questions.question: The graph of y = |x + 3| − 4 crosses the x-axis at two points. How far apart are they?
questions.explanation: On the x-axis y = 0, so |x + 3| = 4: x = 1 or x = −7. They are 1 − (−7) = 8 apart. The arms of the V have slope ±1, so the gap is always twice the depth of the tip below the axis: 2 × 4.
questions.method: Crossing points are the solutions of y = 0.

hints.text: Where the graph crosses the x-axis, y = 0.
Solve |x + 3| = 4.

commonMistakes: Answering 4, the depth of the tip, instead of the width at the axis.

questions.question: Solve |x − 1| > 4.
questions.explanation: x must be more than 4 away from 1: below 1 − 4 = −3 or above 1 + 4 = 5. Two separate pieces, joined by "or".
questions.method: |x − a| > b ⇔ x < a − b or x > a + b.

hints.text: "Greater than" means far from 1, on either side.
Go 4 to the left and 4 to the right of 1, then take the outsides.

commonMistakes: Writing the inside interval −3 < x < 5.
Keeping only x > 5.

questions.question: What is the least value of |x − 2| + |x − 5| + |x − 9| + |x − 14|?
questions.explanation: With four points the sum is least anywhere between the two middle points, 5 and 9. At x = 5: 3 + 0 + 4 + 9 = 16. Pairing outer with outer gives the same: (14 − 2) + (9 − 5) = 12 + 4 = 16.
questions.method: Pair the outermost points, then the next pair, and add the gaps.

hints.text: Group the terms in pairs: the outer two and the inner two.
Each pair is at least the gap between its points.

commonMistakes: Pairing only the outer points (12) and forgetting the inner pair.
Adding all four distances from 0: 2 + 5 + 9 + 14 = 30.

questions.question: How many real solutions does |x − 2| + |x − 6| = 10 have?
questions.explanation: The left side is the total distance from x to 2 and to 6. Its least value is 4 (between 2 and 6); 10 is more than 4, so x lies outside on either side: 2x − 8 = 10 gives x = 9, and 8 − 2x = 10 gives x = −1. Two solutions.
solutionSteps: Least value of the left side: |6 − 2| = 4.
10 > 4, so there is one solution to the right of 6 and one to the left of 2.
questions.method: Compare c with the flat bottom |a − b|.

hints.text: What is the smallest value |x − 2| + |x − 6| can take?
If the target is above the flat bottom, the line y = 10 meets both arms.

commonMistakes: Answering "Infinitely many" because the graph has a flat part; that only happens when c equals the flat value 4.

questions.question: Match each equation with its number of real solutions.
questions.explanation: |x − 3| = 5: x = −2 or 8. |x + 1| = 0: only x = −1. A modulus is never negative, so |x − 2| = −4 has none. |x − 1| + |x − 4| equals 3 for every x from 1 to 4: the flat bottom of the graph lies exactly on y = 3.
solutionSteps: Sum of two distances equal to the gap |4 − 1|: every x in between.
questions.method: Picture the V (or the flat-bottomed graph) and the level line.

hints.text: A modulus can never equal a negative number.
What is |x − 1| + |x − 4| for x = 2? For x = 3?

commonMistakes: Giving |x + 1| = 0 two solutions, ±1.
Giving the flat-bottom case two solutions, x = 1 and x = 4.

questions.question: Solve |x − 4| = 2x + 1.
questions.explanation: Case x ≥ 4: x − 4 = 2x + 1 gives x = −5, which is not ≥ 4, so reject it (also 2x + 1 = −9 < 0, which a modulus can never equal). Case x < 4: 4 − x = 2x + 1 gives x = 1, which fits. Check: |1 − 4| = 3 = 2 + 1. So x = 1 only.
solutionSteps: x ≥ 4: x − 4 = 2x + 1 → x = −5, outside the case: reject.
x < 4: 4 − x = 2x + 1 → x = 1, inside the case: keep.
questions.method: When x appears outside the modulus, solve case by case and check each answer.

hints.text: The right side must not be negative, since a modulus never is.
Substitute each candidate back into the original equation.

commonMistakes: Keeping x = −5 without checking: |−9| = 9 but 2(−5) + 1 = −9.

questions.question: Select ALL the statements that are true.
questions.explanation: (a) 2 < x < 8 holds 3, 4, 5, 6, 7: five integers. (b) A distance is never negative. (c) A modulus cannot be below −1, so no x works. (d) That is the inside interval; |x − 1| > 2 is x < −1 or x > 3. (e) x = 2.5 has |x − 2| = 0.5 < 1 but |x| = 2.5.
questions.method: Turn each modulus into an interval, and look for a counter-example to each claim.

hints.text: For (a), use 2b − 1 for a strict inequality.
For (e), try a value close to 2.

commonMistakes: Counting 2 and 8 in (a), which a strict sign excludes.

questions.question: Five shops stand along a straight road at 2 km, 5 km, 7 km, 12 km and 20 km from Chennai Central. A delivery van will park at one spot on the road, and a runner walks from the van to each shop separately. What is the least possible total of the five one-way distances, in km?
questions.explanation: The total |x − 2| + |x − 5| + |x − 7| + |x − 12| + |x − 20| is least at the median shop, x = 7: 5 + 2 + 0 + 5 + 13 = 25 km.
questions.method: Park at the median shop.

hints.text: Write the total as a sum of five moduli.
With five points the best spot is the third one in order.

commonMistakes: Parking at the mean, 9.2 km, which gives a larger total (27.2 km).

questions.question: How many real solutions does ||x − 3| − 4| = 2 have?
questions.explanation: Remove the outer modulus: |x − 3| − 4 = 2 or −2, so |x − 3| = 6 or |x − 3| = 2. Each gives two solutions: x = 9, −3 and x = 5, 1. Four in all.
questions.method: Peel the moduli from the outside.

hints.text: First remove the outer modulus: what can |x − 3| − 4 be?
Each positive value of |x − 3| gives two values of x.

commonMistakes: Removing both moduli in one go and finding only x = 9 and x = −3.

questions.question: What is the area enclosed by the graph of |x| + |y| = 6?
questions.explanation: The graph is a square with corners (6, 0), (0, 6), (−6, 0) and (0, −6). Its diagonals are 12 long, so the area is 12 × 12 ÷ 2 = 72, that is 2k² with k = 6.
questions.method: A square on its corner: area = d² ÷ 2.

hints.text: Find where the graph meets the axes.
The shape is a square whose diagonals lie on the axes.

commonMistakes: Taking the side as 6 and answering 36.
Using the diagonal as the side and answering 144.

questions.question: How many points with whole-number (integer) coordinates lie on |x| + |y| = 5?
questions.explanation: The four corners (±5, 0), (0, ±5) are on it, plus in each quadrant the points (1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 1) with signs: 4 × 4 = 16. Total 4 + 16 = 20 = 4k.
solutionSteps: Each quadrant: x = 1 to 4, so 4 points, times 4 quadrants = 16.
questions.method: On the square |x| + |y| = k there are 4k integer points.

hints.text: Count the points with x = 0 or y = 0 first.
In the first quadrant, x + y = 5 with x and y both at least 1.

commonMistakes: Counting only one quadrant’s 4 interior points per side and forgetting the corners (16).
Counting the points inside as well (61).

questions.question: For how many integer values of k does the equation ||x| − 3| = k have exactly four real solutions?
questions.explanation: ||x| − 3| = k gives |x| = 3 + k or |x| = 3 − k. Four solutions need both values positive and different: k > 0 and 3 − k > 0, so 0 < k < 3. The integers are 1 and 2. (k = 0 gives 2 solutions, k = 3 gives 3, k > 3 gives 2.)
questions.method: Each positive value of |x| gives two solutions; count the k that make both values positive and distinct.

hints.text: Write the two possible values of |x|.
What happens at k = 0 and at k = 3?

commonMistakes: Including k = 3, where |x| = 0 gives only one solution, so there are three in all.
Including k = 0, where both values coincide.

questions.question: Consider the graph of y = |x² − 4|. Select ALL the statements that are true.

options.text: It meets the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2
It cuts the y-axis at y = 4
The line y = 3 meets it at exactly 4 points
The line y = 5 meets it at exactly 4 points

questions.explanation: The part of y = x² − 4 between −2 and 2 dips below the axis; the modulus reflects it upwards, making a hump of height 4 at x = 0. (a) x² = 4 → x = ±2 ✓. (b) At x = 0, y = |−4| = 4 ✓. (c) x² − 4 = ±3 → x² = 7 or 1 → four points ✓. (d) x² − 4 = ±5 → x² = 9 or −1 → only x = ±3 ✗. (e) A modulus is never negative; the least value is 0 ✗.
solutionSteps: Reflect the dip of x² − 4 above the axis.
y = c meets it at 4 points when 0 < c < 4, 3 points at c = 4, 2 points when c > 4.
questions.method: Reflect the negative part of the graph, then slide a horizontal line.

hints.text: Where is x² − 4 negative? What does the modulus do to that part?
Solve x² − 4 = ±c for c = 3 and c = 5.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the reflected hump and counting only 2 points for y = 3.

questions.question: How many points (x, y) with integer coordinates satisfy |x| + |y| ≤ 4?
questions.explanation: Count by rows. y = 0: |x| ≤ 4 gives 9 points. y = ±1: 7 each. y = ±2: 5 each. y = ±3: 3 each. y = ±4: 1 each. Total 9 + 2(7 + 5 + 3 + 1) = 41 = 2k² + 2k + 1 with k = 4.
questions.method: Count row by row, or use 2k² + 2k + 1.

hints.text: Fix y and count the x that fit: |x| ≤ 4 − |y|.
The rows hold 9, 7, 5, 3, 1 points going up (and the same going down).

commonMistakes: Counting only the boundary (16 points).
Using the area 2k² = 32 as the count.
